tools.name: fly_auth_status
tools.description: Check whether the fly CLI is authenticated and return the current user identity. Returns the email address associated with the active session. If not authenticated, returns authenticated: false — the MCP server cannot perform interactive login; the user must run 'fly auth login' in their terminal first.

tools.name: fly_app_status
tools.description: Get detailed status of a specific app including its deployment state, hostname, and list of machines with their states, regions, and IPs. Use this to check whether an app is deployed and its machines are running before interacting with it.

tools.name: fly_machine_list
tools.description: List all machines (VMs) for a Fly.io app. Each machine entry includes its ID, name, state (started/stopped/suspended/destroyed), region, private IPv6 address, and VM configuration (CPU, memory). Use this to see what's running and get machine IDs for start/stop/destroy operations.

tools.name: fly_machine_start
tools.description: Start a stopped or suspended machine. The machine must already exist and be in a stopped/suspended state. Use fly_machine_list to get the machine ID first.

tools.name: fly_machine_stop
tools.description: Stop a running machine gracefully. The machine is sent a SIGTERM and given time to shut down. Stopped machines can be restarted with fly_machine_start.

tools.name: fly_machine_destroy
tools.description: Permanently destroy a machine. This deletes the VM and its local (non-volume) state. Volumes attached to the machine are NOT destroyed. Use force: true to kill a machine that won't stop gracefully. This cannot be undone.

force.description: Force-kill the machine regardless of current state. Use when a machine is stuck.

tools.name: fly_machine_exec
tools.description:
Execute a single command on a running machine and return its output. Useful for debugging: inspect files, check process state, test connectivity, read environment variables, etc.

This is NOT an interactive shell — the command runs once and output is returned. For complex debugging, chain commands with '&&' or use 'sh -c "..."'.

command.description: The command as an array of arguments. Example: ['ls', '-la', '/app'] or ['sh', '-c', 'ps aux | grep node'].

tools.name: fly_ip_list
tools.description: List all IP addresses allocated to an app. Each entry shows the address, type (private_v6 for Flycast, v4/v6 for public), region, and network. Use this to audit an app's network exposure.

tools.name: fly_ip_release
tools.description: Release (deallocate) an IP address from an app. Use this to remove unwanted IPs discovered via fly_ip_list. Provide the exact IP address string as shown in fly_ip_list output.

tools.name: fly_secrets_list
tools.description: List the names, digests, and creation timestamps of secrets set on an app. Secret VALUES are never returned — only metadata. Use this to verify which secrets are configured before deploying.

tools.name: fly_secrets_set
tools.description:
Set one or more encrypted secrets on an app. Secrets are encrypted at rest and injected as environment variables into machines at boot. By default, setting secrets triggers a redeployment. Use stage: true to set secrets without redeploying.

IMPORTANT: Pass sensitive values (API keys, tokens, passwords) as secrets, NOT as env vars in fly_deploy.

secrets.description: Secrets as KEY: VALUE pairs. Example: { 'DATABASE_URL': 'postgres://...', 'API_KEY': 'sk-...' }.

stage.description: If true, secrets are staged but NOT deployed. They take effect on the next fly_deploy.

tools.name: fly_secrets_unset
tools.description: Remove one or more secrets from an app. The app is redeployed to pick up the change.

tools.name: fly_scale_show
tools.description: Show the current VM size, process groups, and machine counts for an app. Returns CPU kind, CPU count, memory, and how many machines are running per process group and region.

tools.name: fly_scale_count
tools.description: Set the number of machines for an app. Fly.io will create or destroy machines to match the target count. Can be scoped to a specific region or process group. Count is capped at 20 as a safety limit.

count.description: Target number of machines. 0 removes all machines. Max 20.

region.description: Only scale in this region. Without this, scales across all regions.

process_group.description: Only scale this process group (e.g. 'app', 'worker'). Without this, scales the default group.

tools.name: fly_scale_vm
tools.description: Change the VM size for an app's machines. Common sizes: 'shared-cpu-1x', 'shared-cpu-2x', 'shared-cpu-4x', 'performance-1x', 'performance-2x', etc.

memory.description: Override memory in MB. If not set, uses the default for the VM size.

tools.name: fly_volumes_list
tools.description: List all volumes attached to an app. Each entry includes ID, name, size, region, state, and which machine it's attached to.

tools.name: fly_volumes_create
tools.description: Create a persistent volume for an app. Volumes are region-specific and can only be attached to machines in the same region. Encrypted by default. Mount in fly.toml via [[mounts]].

name.description: Volume name. Used in fly.toml [[mounts]] source field. Defaults to 'data'.

region.description: Region to create the volume in (e.g. 'iad'). Must match where machines run.

size_gb.description: Volume size in gigabytes. Default: 1 GB. Max: 500 GB.

tools.name: fly_volumes_destroy
tools.description: Permanently destroy a volume. ALL DATA is lost and cannot be recovered. The 'confirm' parameter must exactly match the volume ID.

confirm.description: Must exactly match the volume_id. Safety confirmation to prevent accidental data loss.

tools.name: fly_config_show
tools.description: Show the merged platform configuration for an app. This is the live config Fly.io is running — fly.toml merged with platform defaults. Includes services, mounts, VM config, env, health checks.

tools.name: fly_logs
tools.description:
Fetch recent log output from an app's machines. Returns the log buffer (not a stream) as structured JSON entries. Can be filtered by region or machine.

For ongoing debugging, call repeatedly — each call fetches the latest buffer. This is a polling pattern, not a stream.

region.description: Filter logs to a specific region.

machine.description: Filter logs to a specific machine ID.

tools.name: fly_app_list
tools.description: List all Fly.io apps in the organization. Each app includes its name, status, and organization. Results exclude ambit infrastructure apps (ambit-* prefix).

org.description: Fly.io organization slug. If omitted and only one org exists, it is used automatically.

tools.name: fly_app_create
tools.description: Create a new Fly.io app on the configured custom private network. The app is created with NO public IPs — it is only reachable via Flycast from the specified private network. After creation, use fly_deploy to deploy code and fly_ip_allocate_flycast to make it reachable. The --network flag is always set to the configured ambit network to ensure the app lives on the correct 6PN.

name.description: Name for the new app. Must be globally unique on Fly.io.

org.description: Fly.io organization slug. If omitted and only one org exists, it is used automatically.

tools.name: fly_app_destroy
tools.description: Permanently destroy a Fly.io app and all its machines, volumes, and IP allocations. This cannot be undone. Cannot target ambit infrastructure apps (ambit-* prefix).

tools.name: fly_deploy
tools.description:
Deploy an app from a Docker image, Dockerfile, or GitHub template.

Template mode: pass a GitHub reference as owner/repo/path[@ref] in the 'template' field. The template is fetched from GitHub, extracted, scanned, and deployed. Mutually exclusive with image and dockerfile.

Safety enforcement:
- --no-public-ips is ALWAYS passed (no public IP allocation)
- --flycast is ALWAYS passed (ensures Flycast private IPv6)
- Pre-flight: fly.toml (from template or local) is scanned for dangerous config patterns (force_https, public TLS handlers)
- Post-flight: fly ips list is checked — any public IPs are released immediately and the deploy is flagged as an error
- Post-flight: fly config show is inspected for exposure signals

Returns an audit result with public IPs found/released, Flycast allocations with their target networks, and config warnings.

app.description: The Fly.io app name to deploy to. Must already exist (use fly_app_create first).

image.description: Docker image to deploy (e.g. 'registry.fly.io/my-app:latest'). Mutually exclusive with dockerfile and template.

dockerfile.description: Path to a Dockerfile to build and deploy. Mutually exclusive with image and template.

template.description: GitHub template reference as owner/repo/path[@ref]. Fetches a template directory from GitHub and deploys it. The template must contain a fly.toml (and typically a Dockerfile). Mutually exclusive with image and dockerfile. Examples: 'ToxicPine/ambit-templates/chromatic', 'ToxicPine/ambit-templates/wetty@v1.0'.

region.description: Primary region for the deployment (e.g. 'iad', 'sea', 'lhr'). Defaults to config region.

strategy.description: Deployment strategy. 'rolling' (default) replaces machines gradually. 'immediate' replaces all at once. 'canary' tests on one machine first. 'bluegreen' spins up a full parallel set.

env.description: Environment variables as KEY: VALUE pairs. NOT secrets — use fly_secrets_set for sensitive values.

build_args.description: Docker build-time arguments as KEY: VALUE pairs. Only used when building from a Dockerfile.

tools.name: fly_ip_allocate_flycast
tools.description:
Allocate a private Flycast IPv6 address for an app, reachable from a specific custom private network. This is the ONLY way to make an app reachable — there is no public IP allocation.

The 'network' parameter is REQUIRED — you must explicitly name which private network will be able to reach this app.

Note: Flycast exposes the app to a DIFFERENT network than the one it lives on. If the app is on network 'alpha' and you allocate with network 'beta', then machines on 'beta' can reach it via '<app>.flycast'.

For ambit setups, the network should typically be the ambit network name so the Tailscale router can reach the app.

network.description: The custom private network that will be able to reach this app via Flycast. REQUIRED.

tools.name: router_list
tools.description:
Discover all ambit subnet routers in the organization. Each router bridges one Fly.io custom private network (6PN) to your Tailscale tailnet. Returns network name, Fly app name, region, machine state, private IP, /48 subnet, and Tailscale device status.

Discovery-based — queries Fly Machines REST API for ambit-* apps on non-default networks, then cross-references with Tailscale.

org.description: Fly.io organization slug. If omitted and only one org exists, it is used automatically.

tools.name: router_status
tools.description:
Detailed status of a specific router by network name. Returns Fly app name, region, machine state, private IPv6, /48 subnet, Tailscale device info (IP, online, advertised/enabled routes), and split DNS.

The network name is the TLD used to reach apps — e.g. 'browsers' means apps are at '<app>.browsers'.

org.description: Fly.io organization slug. If omitted and only one org exists, it is used automatically.

tools.name: router_deploy
tools.description:
Deploy a new Tailscale subnet router to a Fly.io custom private network. Creates the bridge that makes all Flycast apps on the network reachable from your tailnet as '<app>.<network>'.

Steps: create Fly app on custom 6PN → set secrets → deploy router container → wait for tailnet join → configure split DNS → enable accept-routes locally.

Prerequisites: fly CLI authenticated, Tailscale running locally, Tailscale API access token in credential store (~/.config/ambit/credentials.json) or TAILSCALE_API_KEY env var.

network.description: Custom private network name. Becomes the TLD on your tailnet (e.g. 'browsers' → '<app>.browsers').

org.description: Fly.io organization slug. If omitted and only one org exists, it is used automatically.

region.description: Region for the router machine. Default: 'iad'.

tag.description: Tailscale ACL tag for the router. Default: 'tag:ambit-<network>'. Must already exist in tagOwners.

self_approve.description: If true, approve subnet routes via Tailscale API instead of relying on autoApprovers in the ACL policy.

tools.name: router_destroy
tools.description:
Tear down a router for a specific network. Clears split DNS, removes the Tailscale device, destroys the Fly app.

Apps on the network are NOT destroyed — only the router is removed. Re-deploy with router_deploy to restore access.

Reminder: remove the router's tag and autoApprovers entries from your Tailscale ACL policy after destroying.

org.description: Fly.io organization slug. If omitted and only one org exists, it is used automatically.

tools.name: router_doctor
tools.description:
Health checks on a specific router or all routers. Returns pass/fail with remediation hints.

Checks: Tailscale installed, connected, accept-routes enabled, credentials available, router machine running, device visible in tailnet, routes advertised/enabled, split DNS configured.

If network is omitted, checks all discovered routers.

network.description: Specific network to check. If omitted, checks all discovered routers.

org.description: Fly.io organization slug. If omitted and only one org exists, it is used automatically.

tools.name: router_logs
tools.description:
Fetch recent logs from a router's machine. Useful for debugging Tailscale auth, DNS proxy startup, route advertisement, IP forwarding. Router logs use 'Router:' prefix.

Returns the log buffer (not a stream) as structured JSON entries.

org.description: Fly.io organization slug. If omitted and only one org exists, it is used automatically.
